budget.note: Overnight program (Martin, 2026-09-26): 8-hour window; 25 more worker runs and 2 more Opus reviews on top of the pilot's usage.

settled: Representation core = 1-DoF primitives {fixed, revolute, continuous, prismatic}; no helical; floating/planar/ball refused (UnsupportedConstruct), not expanded.
URDF frame convention: joint origin in parent frame, child frame = joint frame at q=0, axis through origin; xyz/rpy stored verbatim as parsed.
Pilot couplings: AffineCoupling only (URDF mimic). Limits stored verbatim on primitives; admissible box derived; conflicts reported (LimitConflict), never clipped.
Tolerances frozen in hand_sampler/grammar_bench/tolerances.py (1e-12 analytic, 1e-10 oracle).
Benchmark lives in hand_sampler/grammar_bench (separate package, separate commits); implementation in hand_sampler/grammar.
Coverage = expressible / in-support inventory, not parse-back derivability (deferred to M2 as constructive reconstruction).
No ContinuumSegment node; Approximation annotations instead; PCC macro deferred to M3.
Oracle references are frozen JSON generated by refgen scripts run in the conda env 'piper' (Pinocchio 3.4.0, MuJoCo 3.2.3); tests run on system Python 3.10.
Purpose: the representation is the substrate for evolution over a grammar, not an importer of real hands. Real hands are in-support/expressiveness checks only; exact matching is not a goal.

Palm-ness is a per-body flag; the palm set is a connected subtree containing the root; a palm joint is an ordinary joint whose child is a palm body. Any number of palm articulation directions; nothing anthropomorphic is assumed.

Palm geometry: convex hull of all palm bodies' capsules at q=0, cut into one convex cell per palm body by a plane through each palm joint origin that contains the joint axis with normal n = d - (d.a)a (d = direction from parent palm joint/root to this joint). Fingers use capsules. Validator: every cell has positive volume; finger mounts lie on their palm body's cell. No geometry genes; mass from cell/capsule volume and one density.
Closed-chain solver deferred to 'only if a production needs it'; the LoopClosure placeholder stays.
Iteration-3 grammar productions: root, palm bodies with optional palm joint (tighter travel than finger joints), finger chains of phalanx capsules, optional intra-finger affine coupling.
Every generated hand has at least one palm body (Martin, 2026-09-25). Import-from-URDF only needs to work; it is not a priority.

Palm cut plane refinement (coordinator, 2026-09-26, to confirm with Martin): plane through the palm joint origin containing its axis, normal = perp_axis(d_child - d_parent) where d_parent is the parent's segment direction toward its tip; sibling overlaps resolved by nearest spine; cells sharing a cut face are adjacent (collision-filtered).

Palm cells (2026-09-26, coordinator after worker counterexample): the plane-carved partition cannot hold for entangled palm trees (seed 10: three palm bodies whose own planes are non-discriminating; no single plane conserves volume and keeps both spines). Replaced by nearest-spine assignment of hull samples, one convex hull per palm body, overlaps allowed only between pairs recorded as adjacent (collision-filtered); coverage and containment asserted, exact partition not claimed. To confirm with Martin.

Representation vs grammar (Martin, 2026-09-26): the representation (structure compiled by derive()) must represent real hands relatively accurately (kinematics only, ~5 mm / 10 deg); the grammar (grids, ranges, priors, operators) is tuned later for explorability. Fitting real hands is an expressivity check only.
The 1e-10/1e-12 tolerances are code-correctness tests (our FK vs Pinocchio/sympy on the same file), not the representation fidelity criterion.

Geometry stays capsules for now; a cross-section study decides whether a single rounded-rectangle template fits most links at acceptable contact cost. Actuation (motors, cross-digit couplings) is future work.
Hand set for the representation check: current 11 + articulated-palm hands (SVH, Shadow, ARMS; SHARPA pinky CMC). Licences not a concern (local dev).
Wrists are never part of the hand (Martin, 2026-09-26): every manifest hand is cut at its palm; ORCA hand_root = right_palm.

One motor per joint (Martin, 2026-09-26): coupled/mimic joints and prismatic joints are future items; the projection keeps every mimic joint as an independent revolute joint with its own declared limits; no prismatic hands are added to the check.

Geometry cross-section (E14, 2026-09-26): keep capsules. On 413 sections from 11 hands a single rounded-rectangle template ties a per-link capsule (41% vs 39% within 3 mm); free per-section rounded rectangles fit ~2x tighter but need per-link shape parameters; no documented PhysX cost advantage. Revisit only with a GPU benchmark (proposal in cross-section-study.md).

RL experiments (Martin, 2026-09-26): stationary palm-up hand, in-hand reorientation, no arm; Martin builds it as a new package isaacsimenvs/inhand_reorient on his own branch. Branch rule (Martin, 2026-09-27): every change stays on martin/hand-grammar and no other branch is ever touched; editing shared files ON THIS BRANCH is allowed (e.g. commit 350cacd, a generic resume hook in pose_reaching_6d/reward_utils/curriculum.py), but prefer keeping changes inside our own packages.

Cluster budget phase 1: <=200 GPU-hours, main tier, <=4 GPUs in flight; preemptible tiers only after resume is verified and with Martin's OK; follow ~/research/slurm/CLAUDE.md etiquette; the agent never attempts cluster logins.

Plan revision (Martin, 2026-09-27): replace E-R1 with a CPU grammar screen (viability + diversity) followed by an evolution pilot (MAP-Elites, shared controller with carried weights, graded fitness, 2 grammar variants x 2 seeds, ~20 GPU-h); E-R0 reduced to local gates + a cluster smoke. See plan-rl-grammar-tuning.md 'Revision, 2026-09-27'.

GPU budget (Martin, 2026-10-01): may exceed 200 GPU-h; do not hog -- match the lab's usage: 4 GPUs continuously on main (SLURM cap) plus resumable runs on the preemptible free-cycles tier as a throttled array (<= 8 in flight); avoid the outlier pattern of dozens of GPUs.

Task spec (Martin, 2026-10-01): use a recent established in-hand rotation task, not our own variant and not the 2021 repose-cube benchmark. Chosen: AnyRotate (Yang et al., CoRL 2024, arXiv 2405.07391): multi-axis rotation about a commanded axis with rolling goals, keypoint + rotation + goal + contact + stability rewards, 20 Hz, 30 s episodes, PPO (rl_games, 8192 envs). Ported from the paper (no code released), palm-up stationary hand, variable hands padded/masked. Optional: NVIDIA Dexsuite (Isaac Lab 2.3, 2025) ADR gravity curriculum behind a flag. Web search budget for this session is exhausted; a 2025-2026 survey needs Martin to raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION.

Task (2026-10-02): task_profile hora -- HORA (Qi et al., CoRL 2022) ported from its released code (z-axis rotation reward clip(w.k, +-0.5) with linvel/pose/torque/work penalties, 1.5 cm fall or 20 s episodes, 20 Hz delta targets a/24, 3-frame proprio history + privileged obs, HORA PPO) plus HORA-style grasp cache. allegro reaches 2.14 rotations per 20 s episode (0.75 rad/s) in 60 min, about HORA's sim level. AnyRotate kept as a faithful port but its lambda_rew curriculum prevents learning here.

Compute location (Martin, 2026-10-02): run all GPU work on the CSAIL cluster; keep the local 4090 free for Martin's other work (CPU-only tests locally are fine). Jobs run from immutable per-commit code snapshots synced to /data/pulkitag/users/mpeticco/code/gm_<sha> with PYTHONPATH shadowing the shared venv's editable install; <= 4 GPUs on main.

Policy architecture (Martin, 2026-10-04): every multi-hand policy (shared controller, evolution populations) uses the team's per-joint token transformer (coevolution/networks/joint_transformer.py layout); padded-MLP multi-hand runs are dropped. Earlier MLP-based population/shared-controller results (pilots 1-3, I41-I44) are historical references only.

rl_games edit approved (Martin, 2026-10-04): flagged, default-off per-design advantage normalisation in third_party/rl_games, in its own 'rl_games (vendored): ...' commits; made via the Edit/Write tools under the project allow rule Edit(//.../third_party/rl_games/**).

issues.decision: Fixed in 12fd6ab. Root cause: the palm-up calibration scored stability near the palm ORIGIN, so it chose fingers-down with the cube on the wrist face (0/300 random joint sweeps brought any SHARPA fingertip within 3 cm); also flat default pose, action mapping centred on limit midpoints, stale EMA targets after partial resets, curriculum-ignoring first goal, 0.10 m drop threshold. issues.decision: Root cause: SAPG expl_reward_type=entropy silently applies an entropy coefficient 0.001 (a2c_common.py:345, a2c_continuous.py:159-163) overriding entropy_coef 0; in populations most action dims are ghost slots whose noise does not affect the advantage, actions saturate beyond std 1, and adaptive lr climbs to 1e-2, so log-std drifts up without bound; weight growth then overflowed fp16 (mu 5.85e5), GradScaler collapsed to scale 0, and PyTorch's unscale_ turned 0*inf into NaN weights at gen 7. No design produced non-finite physics. Fix: InHandReorientPopSAPG.yaml (expl_reward_type none; inhand_actor_critic network with logstd_max 0), driver retry/finite-checkpoint/scaler-reset/sigma-on-carry/norm-count-cap, env NaN guard. 3-gen validation: std 1.00 -> 0.73, probes roughly doubled, successes .019 -> .074. Competence still low (holding more than rotating).

issues.hypothesis: Populations under HORA: train only on designs with a stable grasp; per-generation grasp search with offspring viability logged as a grammar metric; validate that a shared controller learns rotation across viable hands. UPDATE (eeab80f..07a833b, 417 tests): --viable-only driver works on the cluster (gen 0 50 min incl. 29 min grasp search at 7.7% founder viability for G_V3S, later gens 30 min with 66% offspring viability). No shared controller learned (mixed32, sub8: holding ~0.4 s). Decisive control: the grammar-path allegro ALONE plateaus at ~2 s holding vs 17.8 s for the URDF allegro -> the grammar-path hand construction is the bottleneck (actuator, capsule colliders and radius 0.01 m, no palm colliders (I30), placement). Vibrating grasps now rejected (joint speed > 5 rad/s). UPDATE (5f89f06..cad1d6e, 429 tests, ~7.65 GPU-h on ada6000-shared): the grammar-path allegro learns alone when its grasp cache uses HORA's canonical pose (10.9 s holding, 0.98 rotations/episode at 30 min); construction factors were roughly neutral (HORA actuator vibrates on capsules; the palm hull as built blocks the thumb). Sharing is the blocker: allegro + founder 174 under one controller both stall at ~1-2 s. Next: morphology context in observations (the HORA port dropped the per-joint descriptors), per-design reward/advantage normalisation, per-design canonical grasp search.

Shared HORA controller over two viable hands fails (14 variants, ~7.95 GPU-h): allegro in the pair <= 2.1 s holding vs 10.5 s solo at the same env count. Ruled out: env/multi-design path (zero-action holds 17 s / 13 s in the pair), morphology context, per-design reward norm, opposition grasps, ghost masks, disjoint policy columns + separate critic, minibatch, optimiser/KL. A non-viable partner (every episode a 0.1 s drop) hurts as much -> sharing the batch itself breaks learning. Trained policies hold for less time than zero actions; allegro's own log-std stays high (-0.84 vs -1.41 solo). Coordinator hypothesis: batch-global advantage normalisation (and value/input normalisers) rescales each design's signal; untested because it needs a flagged change in the vendored rl_games. Literature: GET-Zero (2024) handles multi-embodiment in-hand rotation by per-embodiment experts distilled into one graph transformer. UPDATE: editing third_party/rl_games (per-design advantage norm) was denied by the permission classifier; not retried, awaiting Martin. Config arms: low initial log-std (-1.75) and value/input normalisers off -> allegro still ~1.6-1.8 s; drops come from mean actions, not exploration noise. Next: per-design subnetworks inside our own policy_network.py to separate network interference from PPO-level coupling. UPDATE (4dff083, f66d6e4, 1ebd933; 449 tests; ~4.9 GPU-h): coupling = shared weights AND the pooled input normaliser (allegro's joint columns compressed 2-5x by pooled std). Per-design networks + per-design input normalisation: allegro in the pair 7.1 s at 20 min, 14.2 s / 1.41 rotations at 30 min (solo 13.2 s); founder 174 then slips 2.0 -> 1.0 s, likely PPO batch statistics (advantage norm, KL-adaptive lr, grad clip). Shared trunk + per-design heads + input norm: 2.9 s. 4 hands at 1024 envs each: no learning in 40 min. Next test (per-design advantage normalisation) needs the denied rl_games edit.

Shared-policy theories experiment (Martin, 2026-10-04): port the team's per-joint token + transformer policy (coevolution/networks/joint_transformer.py; 32 values per joint token: proprio history, link box, limits + enabled, object keypoints) to task_profile hora with a raw enabled mask and valid-token normalisation; compare T0 MLP, T1 transformer, T2 + per-design input stats, T3 hand curriculum / warm start, T4 more samples, T5 per-design advantage norm (only if Martin approves the rl_games edit), T6 GET-Zero-style distillation from grammar_solo experts; 2 -> 4 -> 8 hands, metric = fraction of each hand's solo performance; held-out zero-shot for the best arm. UPDATE 2026-10-04: token transformer ported (c973181 etc.) and made the driver default (3c3141b); 40-120 min runs with an MLP-tuned HORA recipe failed even solo (allegro 0.5-0.6 s); pair holds up to ~6-8 s with more samples but ~0.15 rotations. The collaborator's working recipe differs: lr 1e-4 (ours hit the 1e-2 cap), e_clip 0.1, 2 mini-epochs, d_model 128, SAPG 6 blocks, 24,576 envs, ~2 B steps per generation (ours ~0.06-0.2 B). Fair test launched: their recipe (R1 plain PPO, R2 + SAPG) on solo allegro for 6 h vs an MLP reference, then pair/4 hands incl. group advantage norm (e4dee41, a991fae).

GET-Zero-style pipeline (Patel & Song 2024): ~8 training hands (allegro, sharpa, leap projections + ~5 viable grammar designs) get solo MLP experts under HORA; DAgger distillation into the token transformer; evaluate student vs expert on training hands and zero-shot vs zero-action floor on 2-4 held-out hands. RESULT 1 (8087f66..2ed376e, ~9 GPU-h): DAgger distillation into the token transformer reaches 94-105% of each of 6 experts; allegro student 13.3 s / 1.27 rotations (first transformer to do the task; 8x the RL transformer). But 5/6 experts flick-and-drop (0.3-1.8 s vs 14.5-18.9 s zero-action) because their grasp caches were palm-up seeded, so held-out zero-shot is 2-29% of the zero-action time. Next: opposition-seeded grasp caches for all candidates, stricter expert keep rule (>= 50% of zero-action holding and >= 0.3 rotations), redistil on 8+ hands across all grammar variants, >= 4 held-out hands.
